newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe stocks end week firmer in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe stocks end week firmer in active trade.

text.p: Zimbabwe industrials rallied to close the week firmer on Friday, backing brokers' earlier predictions that their lapse during the week was a temporary setback.
"Today was confirmation that the fundamentals in the market are still pretty strong. We have quite a bit of money chasing stocks," one broker commented.

"With inflation and interest rates coming down people can now afford to make productive investments. The stock market provides a very attractive home for investors in the present conditions," he said.
He said more foreigners were creeping into the market as the Zimbabwe dollar continued depreciating against the key U.S. dollar.
"The Zimbabwe dollar has also devaluated quite a bit against the U.S. dollar and that should attract a lot of foreigners," the broker said.
The 57-counter industrial index added 34.37 points to 1,006.62 on Friday although it lost 126.37 points on the week.

The day's major advances were in Edgars which pushed 250 cents up to 4,900, and Chemco, 100 cents stronger at 4,600. Meikles put on 50 cents to 2,200, Caps gained 25 cents to 875 and udc and Afdis both went up 20 cents to 350 and 550 respectively.
Minings traded largely unchanged with the seven-share secondary index losing 27.68 points to finish at 885.70, 27.68 points down on the week.
